clue.text: Rake moved faster

indicators.note: the letters of the word beside it are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rake, perhaps a garden tool or a racehorse, that went more quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake a target is to sweep it with gunfire, which is what fighter planes do when they strafe.

clue.text: No chores undone in this vessel

indicators.note: chores left undone suggests their letters are unravelled and reformed

explanation.surface: Life aboard ship is free of housework.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging on two or more masts.

clue.text: As I put in the letter, I have private means

indicators.note: I is put inside the word for someone who lets property

parts.note: a letter here is someone who lets property, a renter

explanation.surface: Someone writes in a letter that they are independently wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is not an alphabet letter but one who lets. The definition is the answer speaking for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living on income from property or investments rather than work.

clue.text: A sportsman on the ball, Jeremy

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or alert, on the ball
Jeremy Fisher is the frog who goes fishing in Beatrix Potter's children's story

explanation.surface: A sportsman named Jeremy is sharp on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler using artificial flies, someone who goes after fish for sport.

clue.text: Sings the praises of vintage drink

parts.note: vintage means classic, top quality, as does crack (a crack shot)
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone extols a fine old wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up something is an idiom for praising it highly, talking it up.

clue.text: Arachnologist has to dress right but cheer wrong

parts.note: to robe is to dress

indicators.note: the words but cheer are put wrong, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A spider expert must dress correctly but cheer at the wrong moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link; 'wrong' rearranges BUT CHEER to THEBRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish king is said to have watched a spider persevere in spinning its web, a jocular spider-studier.

clue.text: Rent collected from Conservative and Socialist

parts.note: a socialist is on the political left

explanation.surface: A landlord collects rent from tenants of both parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected from' is a link; 'Rent' means a tear, not a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a split or fissure, a crack.

clue.text: Subordinate part of a sentence

explanation.surface: A dependent clause in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of the crown is ruled over; in grammar it is the noun the verb is about.

clue.text: I enrolled in association to get equal pay

indicators.note: I joins and so sits inside the association

parts.note: a party is a political association

explanation.surface: I joined a union to win equal pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality, especially of pay between groups.

clue.text: A biblical character, Japheth, got involved with O.T. bints

indicators.note: the letters are tangled together into a new order

parts.note: OT is short for the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Noah's son Japheth got mixed up with some girls from the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' and 'with' are links; bints is British slang for girls.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament prophet who baptised Jesus.

clue.text: Make inroads in the sweet store

explanation.surface: A child raids the sweet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to riddle with holes or tunnels; as a noun it is the waxy cells where bees keep their honey.

clue.text: Always gets doctor in the aftermath of fire

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters inside the poetic word for always

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is always called after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal is what remains after the flames of a fire die down.

clue.text: Vegetation obscuring very good view

indicators.note: the vegetable covers and so hides the short word for very good, which sits within it

parts.note: an onion is a vegetable, loosely vegetation
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: Plants block a fine view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a belief or judgement someone holds.

clue.text: Den to give ground

explanation.surface: A lair into which an animal backs off.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a private hideaway or bolt-hole; to give ground is to withdraw or fall back.

clue.text: Ditto

parts.note: ditto repeats the clue above, so this clue also reads 'Den': the home of a fox

explanation.walkthrough: Ditto means 'the same again': the clue is just 13 across's 'Den' repeated, here the burrow a fox lives in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's den is called by this name, so it shares the previous clue's definition.

clue.text: Before this smash, other smashes

parts.note: to smash a ball is to hit it hard

indicators.note: the word other is smashed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Before this big success, others had flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashes' rearranges OTHER to HERTO, placed after HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Means up until now, previously, before the present moment.

clue.text: Dancer's bound to ask about Charleston's first two steps

indicators.note: the plea goes around the opening pair of letters

parts.note: to entreat is to ask earnestly

indicators.note: take only the opening two letters of Charleston

explanation.surface: A dancer is bound to ask for the opening steps of the Charleston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'obliged' but is a leap; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the feet several times in mid-air.

clue.text: Blocks the way in — leaves

indicators.note: the street abbreviation goes in the French leaves

parts.note: a conge is a leave or permission to depart, from French
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Something obstructs the entrance and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To block is to clog or choke up, as traffic does a road.

clue.text: You might think this nail non-essential

definitions.text: You might think this nail non-essential

parts.words: You might think this nail non-essential
parts.note: the name of this shoemaker's nail sounds as if it describes something that can be spared

explanation.walkthrough: A sparable is a small headless nail used by shoemakers; the name looks like 'spare-able', something you could do without.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's sprig or small nail, whose name suggests 'able to be spared', dispensable.

clue.text: Friend failed to speak — he could tell you a lot

definitions.text: he could tell you a lot

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: the word is said out loud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: missed means failed

explanation.surface: A friend fell silent, though he knew a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' means your lot in life, your fate, which a palm reader foretells.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller who reads destiny from the hand.

clue.text: Transient round for a time

parts.note: a temp is a transient, short-term worker
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A passing visitor stops for a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In music it is the speed or pace, and musicians call that the time.

clue.text: Old gold suit in silk

indicators.note: the word for suit goes inside the watered silk

parts.note: moire is watered silk
to do is to suit, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: An old golden suit made of silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portuguese gold coin, once current in England.

clue.text: I have little colour and .

clue.text: Nancy gets as much money as possible out of work

parts.words: gets as much money as possible out of
parts.note: to milk someone is to exploit them for all you can get
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Nancy takes every penny from her job.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name; here it is old slang for a weak or effeminate man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated insults for a timid, unmanly man.

clue.text: … stick to the point

parts.note: read as a staff with a sharp tip, or a verb meaning to pierce

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a discussion relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: This continues 22 down; 'stick to the point' reads as advice to stay relevant, but describes a pointed stick, or the act of stabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon made of a shaft with a sharp head, and as a verb to pierce with one.

clue.text: Fetid — needs venting, we hear

indicators.note: says the next word sounds the same when spoken as the entry

parts.note: wreaking anger is venting it

explanation.surface: Something smelly needs airing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetid means foul-smelling, stinking strongly.

clue.text: Passionate amour abandoned by Fanny Adams

indicators.note: the letters of Fanny Adams drop out of the love affair, leaving it behind

parts.note: an amour is a love affair, in French spelling affaire
sweet Fanny Adams, abbreviated FA, is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A love affair ends when Fanny Adams walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F and A from AFFAIRE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ardent or fired up with feeling is figuratively ablaze.

clue.text: Conspiring with a king? Och!

parts.note: the Inca was the king of the Inca people of Peru
och and hoots are both Scottish exclamations of impatience

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims when someone teams up with royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in league with someone, plotting together.

clue.text: Being without note, some say

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the being goes round the note

parts.note: an entity is a being, something that exists
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Life without music, as some would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken: 'some' said aloud is 'sum', a total or whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the total amount, the whole of something.

clue.text: When? About that time? Capital!

indicators.note: the word for when is placed around the words for that time

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
then means at that time

explanation.surface: Someone asks when something happened, and then exclaims 'Excellent!'
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital city.
